findings.summary: The hollow grey label-axis marker is drawn at the same 6.5 pt size directly over the filled red solved-axis marker, so the pair renders as one red triangle with a grey rim rather than as two nulls. A reader cannot tell from this panel that both null sets mark the same point: the filled shape reads as outlined (its own style is contradicted) and the hollow marker's own style is not visible at all, so the comparison this panel exists to support -- solved axis against EFIT label axis -- is not readable from the marks. The other four panels separate the two markers by 10 to 55 px and read correctly, so this is a coincident-null rendering defect, not a legend or vocabulary defect. Recorded as non-blocking: the field, the wall and every contour remain readable, and the coincidence itself is the finding a reader would want, just not one the mark style lets them see.

findings.evidence: image-0.png through image-4.png, 1400x720; dashed domain bound at x 566-833, y 115-619 on every panel; figsize at scripts/prototypes/diiid_forward_convergence/render_panels.py:507 and equal aspect from nova/media/ink.py:164
findings.summary: The 14 x 7.2 canvas is 1.94:1 while the DIII-D poloidal box is tall and narrow, and equal aspect keeps the shape honest, so the drawn panel occupies only 268 px of the 1400 px width (19 percent; about 13 percent of the canvas area) and roughly 81 percent of the width is empty white. At the delivered size the nine-level contour fields are thin: a reader gets a small picture in a large frame, and the emphasis the figure can carry is limited by how little room the data occupy. The five panels also spend that width on nothing that would help the reading -- the brief asks for a per-frame residual trajectory against Newton promotions, which this empty band could hold beside each map.

findings.evidence: image-0.png through image-4.png; scripts/prototypes/diiid_forward_convergence/render_panels.py:518-546; nova/media/ink.py flux_color/flux_linewidth (#3366cc, 0.7) and contour_color (#999999)
findings.summary: The EFIT label field is drawn after the solved field and heavier, so the reference carries more visual weight than the subject. The solved contours are drawn first at the ink default 0.7 pt in #3366cc (line 518) and the label contours are drawn over them at an explicit 1.0 pt in #999999 (lines 537-546); where the two coincide the grey dominates and the solved series reads as the paler, partially covered one. The repository rule puts the subject on top and drawn heavier; here the emphasis is inverted, which matters on these five panels because the solved field is the evidence and the label is the reference it is judged against.

findings.summary: The legend swatches are drawn at weights the figure does not use: Nova solved flux at 1.6 pt against a plotted 0.7 pt, EFIT label flux at 1.2 against 1.0, and solved separatrix at 1.2 against 1.5. The first two make the data series look heavier in the legend than on the panel, and the separatrix reads lighter in the legend than the strong red curve a reader is meant to follow. A legend entry that does not match its line is a small but avoidable misdescription of the encoding.

findings.evidence: image-0.png through image-4.png at 2x and 4x; marker and separatrix colours at nova/media/ink.py (xpoint_color and separatrix_color both #cc0000); draw at scripts/prototypes/diiid_forward_convergence/render_panels.py:527-536 and :558-564
findings.summary: The solved saddle is marked in the same red (#cc0000) as the solved separatrix contour that passes through it, so the marker sits on a line of its own colour and reads as a thickening of that line rather than as a distinct null. This is visible on all five panels -- most clearly on frame 146, where the cross merges into the open red curve -- and it costs the reader the comparison the house vocabulary exists for: the saddle's position relative to the axis and the wall. A contrasting edge or a darker fill on the marker would keep the null vocabulary intact without changing what is drawn.

The caption's fixed-width wrap splits a parenthetical across its two lines on frame 146 -- 'axis inside limiter NO (plasma outside the' ends line one and 'vessel)' opens line two -- so the most consequential clause of that caption is broken in the middle of the phrase. The text is not clipped and remains readable, but the break lands inside the explanation rather than between the clauses the ' | ' separator already delimits.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: The captions do not merely repeat a title: each figure carries no title, and the caption names the frame, the diverted terminal residual, the converged flag, the axis position and whether it lies inside the limiter, the closed-core cell count, the confined-current ratio and the tolerance. The identity is in the file name and the caption, as the repository convention requires.
item_verdicts.finding_materiality: Six findings, none blocking. No text is clipped (0 non-white pixels in the outer 3 px frame of every render), no text overlaps another text or the data, all text is near-black on white, and no figure depicts tabular information. The defects recorded are encoding and emphasis defects that reduce what a reader can take from the marks; none prevents the panel from being read.
item_verdicts.rendered_artifact: Five attached PNGs were opened with Read and inspected at native size and in upscaled crops (2x panels, 4x null regions, 10x coincident markers). No SVG was opened, read or rendered.
